findings.F1: The Calmar fails at 0.70 because the deepest fall is −32.8 % against a yearly return of +23.4 %; that fall took 362 days across w1–w4, while holding the coins fell −60.7 %. The next falls are −24.2 % (w21–w22, holding −39.4 %), −19.8 % (w20–w21, holding −3.8 %) and −18.9 % (w12–w13, holding −70.2 %).
findings.F2: Inside the six deepest falls the book stays invested on 61 % of bars (72 % elsewhere) at a mean allocation of 0.40 (0.48 elsewhere). Its active bars there lose −0.19 % per bar over 3294 bars, against +0.22 % per bar over 8584 bars outside the falls. The coin's next-day return on those bars is −0.50 %, against +0.38 % outside.
findings.F3: The falls are flat months sitting inside a longer decline. On active fall bars the coin's median 30-day return is +0.4 % (+9.3 % elsewhere). Its median 90-day return is −4.1 % (+15.9 % elsewhere), and its median distance below the 90-day high is −21.3 % (−10.3 % elsewhere). The 30-day flatness factor cannot see this 90-day downtrend.
findings.F4: Active bars within 3.4 % of the 90-day high gain +0.197 % per bar (t 2.9, 1851 bars), and only 10 % of them fall inside the book's falls. Bars 18–33 % below that high gain +0.008 % (t 0.2), and 40 % of them fall inside the book's falls. The deepest quintile, more than 33 % below, gains +0.147 % (t 3.1) but also has 42 % of its bars inside the falls.
findings.F5: Being below or above the 50-day mean does not separate the losses. Inside the falls, bars below it lose −0.17 % per bar (2235 bars) and bars above it lose −0.25 % per bar (1059 bars).
findings.F6: The gain is concentrated in the strongest signals and the strongest recent pushes. Forecasts of 12.2 or more earn +0.32 % per bar (t 4.0) and carry 7.5 of the 14.8 summed gain, while forecasts below 6 earn about +0.04 %. Bars after a past 5-day rise above 8.6 % earn +0.25 % per bar (t 3.9), against +0.006 % after a 5-day move of −5 % to −0.7 %.
findings.F7: The idea's unusual move is +0.34 % per 5-day case, 1.8 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The thin margin left to holding comes mostly from the drift (+0.59 %), and that drift turns negative in the 90-day declines where the falls occur.

ideas.idea: The farther a coin's close sits above the middle of its 30-day closing range, the larger its rise over the next 5 days; the flatter the 30 days were, the larger that rise, and the closer the close stands to its 90-day high, the larger that rise again.
ideas.consequence: A close near the top of a flat month is a reason to buy for 5 days when the coin is near its 90-day high, and a weak one when the flat month sits well below that high.
ideas.name: flat range near highs

ideas.idea: The farther a coin's close sits above the middle of its 30-day closing range, the larger its rise over the next 5 days; the flatter the 30 days were, the larger that rise, and the larger the coin's rise over the past 5 days that carried it there, the larger that rise again.
ideas.consequence: A sharp 5-day push toward the top of a flat month is a reason to buy for the next 5 days, while a drift to the same place gives little reason to.
ideas.name: pushed range top continuation
